data.title: Premium SMS Billing Anomaly — Unauthorized Premium SMS Subscriptions Appearing on Accounts
data.description: Detects unauthorized premium SMS subscriptions (cramming) appearing on customer accounts without corresponding opt-in or consent records. Premium SMS cramming generates an estimated $1.5B in unauthorized consumer charges annually (CFCA/TNS 2026). Fraudsters add premium SMS shortcode subscriptions to accounts through compromised billing APIs, social engineering of carrier support staff, or malware-initiated WAP billing triggers. The key detection signal is premium SMS subscription records that lack a corresponding customer opt-in event. Multiple premium subscriptions appearing on the same account within a 30-day window without opt-in are high-confidence cramming indicators.

enrichment_required.source: Customer consent management system — presence of explicit opt-in for the specific shortcode
Count of new premium SMS subscriptions per account in 30-day window
Account tenure derived from activation date

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Premium SMS Billing Anomaly — DL-0185")`
`comment("Detects unauthorized premium SMS subscriptions appearing on accounts")`
index=flame_telecom sourcetype=flame:billing
  (charge_type="premium_sms" OR charge_type="premium_content"
   OR charge_type="shortcode_subscription")
| lookup premium_sms_opt_in account_id, shortcode OUTPUT opt_in_date, opt_in_channel
| where isnull(opt_in_date)
| bin _time span=30d
| stats dc(shortcode) as unique_shortcodes,
        count as charge_count,
        sum(charge_amount) as total_charges,
        values(shortcode) as shortcodes,
        values(content_provider) as content_providers,
        values(billing_source) as billing_sources,
        earliest(subscription_start_date) as first_subscription,
        latest(subscription_start_date) as last_subscription
  by account_id, customer_name, _time
| where unique_shortcodes >= 2
| eval risk_score = case(
    unique_shortcodes >= 5 AND total_charges > 100, "critical",
    unique_shortcodes >= 3 AND total_charges > 50, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table account_id, customer_name, unique_shortcodes, charge_count,
        total_charges, shortcodes, content_providers, billing_sources,
        first_subscription, last_subscription, risk_score
| sort - unique_shortcodes
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Premium SMS Billing Anomaly Detection
-- Detects unauthorized premium SMS subscriptions without opt-in records
SELECT
  a.account_id,
  a.customer_name,
  a.account_open_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.shortcode) AS unique_shortcodes,
  COUNT(*) AS charge_count,
  SUM(s.charge_amount) AS total_charges,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT s.shortcode, ', ') AS shortcodes,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT s.content_provider, ', ') AS content_providers,
  MIN(s.subscription_start_date) AS first_subscription,
  MAX(s.subscription_start_date) AS last_subscription,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT s.shortcode) >= 5 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT s.shortcode) >= 3 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_score
FROM customer_accounts a
JOIN premium_sms_subscriptions s ON a.account_id = s.account_id
LEFT JOIN premium_sms_opt_in o ON a.account_id = o.account_id
                               AND s.shortcode = o.shortcode
WHERE s.subscription_start_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND o.opt_in_id IS NULL
GROUP BY a.account_id, a.customer_name, a.account_open_date
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.shortcode) >= 2
ORDER BY total_charges DESC
queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Premium SMS Billing Anomaly
(charge_type="premium_sms" OR charge_type="premium_content"
 OR charge_type="shortcode_subscription")
| !has_opt_in_record
| groupBy(account_id, customer_name, function=[
    countDistinct(shortcode, as=unique_shortcodes),
    count(as=charge_count),
    sum(charge_amount, as=total_charges),
    collect([shortcode, content_provider, billing_source]),
    min(subscription_start_date, as=first_subscription),
    max(subscription_start_date, as=last_subscription)
  ], span=30d)
| unique_shortcodes >= 2
| sort(total_charges, order=desc)

references: Subex, Global Telecom Fraud Intelligence Report (2025, 2026)
falsepositives: Customers who legitimately subscribed to multiple premium SMS services via web or app opt-in flows not captured in the consent management system
Promotional trials that auto-convert to paid subscriptions after consent was given verbally
Partner-bundled premium services included with certain plan types
Consent records delayed due to system synchronization lag between opt-in platform and billing
